newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says no baht, finance portfolio changes.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says no baht, finance portfolio changes.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh reaffirmed on Thursday that Thailand has no plan to devalue its currency and that he would keep his Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan, a government minister said.

A minister in the prime minister's office said Chavalit made the comments to a meeting of senior economic and finance officials. Chavalit told them he would help Amnuay coordinate government policies as the country deals with its economic downturn, which has triggered attacks on the baht and heavy selling on the stock market.

"The prime minister confirmed that there would be no change in the finance ministerial post. It is just a rumour...under the current circumstances, there would be no baht devaluation," said Minister Bhokin Bhalakula of the Prime Minister's Office.

Market fears that some members in Chavalit's coalition government may call for Amnuay's resignation to take responsibility for economic problems, helped trigger attacks on the baht and caused Thai stocks to plunge on Wednesday.

The baht firmed on Thursday following assurances by Amnuay and the Bank of Thailand that there were no plans to devalue the baht or change the exchange rate mechanism. The baht was trading around 25.800/25.830 to the dollar at mid-morning compared with 26.330/26.430 late on Wednesday.
Amnuay also denied he was stepping down from his post.
Bhokin said Chavalit could help Amnuay coordinate policies of various agencies outside the jurisdiction of the finance ministry.
He said Chavalit's economic advisers from different coalition parties also pledged to cooperate in implementing policies adopted by the government.

Analysts said the Chart Pattana Party, the second biggest coalition partner led by former Prime Minister Chatichai Choonhavan, favours more liberal fiscal and monetary measures to lift Thailand out of its current economic downturn.
